---
title: "Troubleshooting: typed errors, missing values, and resource limits"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Troubleshooting: typed errors, missing values, and resource limits}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
---

`readboj` fails closed through documented validation, transport, parser,
cache, and resource checks when an input or source is not trustworthy. These
expected failures retain a specific `readboj_*_error` class, so a pipeline can
handle them without matching a fragile message string. An unexpected base or
dependency error can still surface from manually malformed cache metadata or
a third-party file; preserve the input identity and report that case.

All default examples here are local and deterministic. The package fixtures
are synthetic and are labelled as such; they do not stand in for official BOJ
values.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 78)
library(readboj)

fixture_file <- function(name) {
  path <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "readboj")
  if (!nzchar(path)) {
    candidates <- c(file.path("inst", "extdata", name),
      file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", name))
    path <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)][1L]
  }
  if (!nzchar(path) || !file.exists(path)) stop("Fixture is unavailable: ", name)
  normalizePath(path, mustWork = TRUE)
}

capture_error <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(
    list(ok = TRUE, value = force(expr)),
    error = function(error) list(
      ok = FALSE,
      class = class(error),
      message = conditionMessage(error)
    )
  )
}
```

## Identify a typed condition

An empty offline cache is a useful way to test a network policy without
contacting the BOJ service. The failure is explicit and machine-readable:

```{r offline-error}
offline_failure <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08",
  code = "SYNTHM01",
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-empty-cache-"),
  offline = TRUE,
  wait = 0
))
offline_failure$class[1L]
offline_failure$message
```

The usual response is to check the cache path, the canonical query, and the
`max_age` setting. If a connected refresh is permitted, rerun with
`refresh = TRUE`; otherwise keep the call offline and report that the required
snapshot is absent.

Input errors are separate from source availability. For example, duplicate
series codes and reversed period bounds are rejected before any network
request:

```{r parameter-errors}
duplicate_codes <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08", code = c("SYNTHM01", "SYNTHM01"),
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-no-request-"), offline = TRUE, wait = 0
))
reversed_period <- capture_error(read_boj_series(
  db = "FM08", code = "SYNTHM01",
  start_date = "202603", end_date = "202601",
  cache_dir = tempfile("readboj-no-request-"), offline = TRUE, wait = 0
))
c(duplicate = duplicate_codes$class[1L], reversed = reversed_period$class[1L])
```

Handle these as configuration or user-input issues. Do not retry a
`readboj_parameter_error` as if it were a transient transport problem.

## Distinguish size and schema failures

Every parser accepts a bound. A deliberately tiny byte bound raises a size
condition before parsing starts:

```{r size-error}
size_failure <- capture_error(read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"),
  type = "data_json",
  db = "FM08",
  max_bytes = 10L
))
size_failure$class[1L]
size_failure$message
```

The same principle applies to API cells/pages/codes, metadata rows, bulk ZIP
entries and bytes, and workbook sheets/rows/columns/cells. Increase a bound
only when the job's memory and time budget supports it. API and archive readers
do not silently return a partial table after crossing a declared limit.

Malformed or changed BOJ response fields raise `readboj_schema_error`;
HTTP/API failures use more specific classes such as
`readboj_transport_error`, `readboj_auth_error`, or `readboj_api_error`.
Successful response bodies are cached only after transport and size checks
pass, so a failed response should not become a valid offline object.

## Preserve missing-value markers

Missing values have different representations in different official formats.
The synthetic JSON fixture contains `null`, while the CSV fixture contains an
empty field:

```{r missing-markers}
json <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"), type = "data_json", db = "FM08"
)
csv <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-en-page-1.csv"),
  type = "data_csv", db = "FM08", language = "en"
)

json[is.na(json$value), c("period", "value", "raw_value", "value_status")]
csv[!nzchar(csv$raw_value), c("period", "value", "raw_value", "value_status")]
```

JSON missing values are labelled `"null"`; blank CSV cells are labelled
`"blank"`. `read_boj_bulk()` additionally retains source strings such as
`"NA"` and `"ND"` in its `value` column and reports their marker in
`value_status`. Treat these statuses as source semantics rather than replacing
all missing-looking values with zero.

## Encoding, credentials, and network checks

Japanese metadata and CSV responses use CP932 in the official interface. Pass
the encoding explicitly when parsing a local response, and inspect both
bilingual fields:

```{r encoding}
japanese <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("metadata-bilingual-cp932.csv"),
  type = "metadata_csv",
  db = "FM08",
  encoding = "CP932"
)
japanese[japanese$is_series, c("series_code", "name_en", "name_jp")]
```

The BOJ API is public: `readboj` has no credential argument and does not
write secrets to URLs, cache indexes, or provenance. Requests use HTTPS and
official BOJ hosts only. If an explicitly opted-in live call fails, first
inspect the condition class, then distinguish a temporary network/rate-limit
condition from an API error, authorization rejection, schema change, or local
resource limit. Keep
`offline = TRUE` in automated builds and use separately cached runs with
`READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true` for live refreshes.

For the prescribed credit string, API notice, copyright link, and service
release contact, inspect `boj_api_credit()` rather than copying a stale string
into a report:

```{r credit}
credit <- boj_api_credit()
credit[c("credit", "api_notice", "copyright", "service_release_contact")]
```
